page: Amazon Web Services c3.large is a compute-optimized, third-generation instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is built on the Xen hypervisor and uses the i386 CPU architecture. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, providing 1.88 GB per core, and includes 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There are no GPUs bundled with this configuration, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the c3.large in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is weak at 1263.58, while the multi-core CPU score drops to the bottom 10% at 1640.98. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.06 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.39 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect these constraints, yielding a single-core score of 702.0 and a multi-core score of 812.0. Cryptographic and compression tasks show similar limitations, with a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 788.22 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.35 GB/sec.

Given its legacy hardware profile, the c3.large offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated compute resources, though it exhibits low resource density and performance-per-resource efficiency compared to newer generations. The inclusion of 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast local read/write access, but the lack of baseline network bandwidth limits its utility for distributed systems. This instance is best suited for legacy applications, basic web serving, lightweight single-threaded tasks, or small-scale development and testing environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory or modern instruction sets like AVX-512.
